column3: Shagbark hickory (Carya ovata), a true hickory, clear straight-grained small specimens at 12% moisture content
column4: FPL-GTR-282 Table 5-3a (metric), true hickories, 12% row: specific gravity 0.72 (footnote b: ovendry weight, volume at 12% moisture content); static bending modulus of elasticity 14,900 MPa from a simply supported, center-loaded beam at span/depth 14 (footnote c: increase by 10% to correct for shear deflection)
column5: Average clear-wood values, not a particular drumstick; drumstick hickory is sold without a species, and the four true hickories at 12% moisture content span specific gravity 0.69 to 0.75 and bending MOE 13,000 to 15,600 MPa (mockernut 0.72 and 15,300, pignut 0.75 and 15,600, shellbark 0.69 and 13,000; stored below). The isotropic young_modulus is the pack author's reduction for a Hertz stick tip: the longitudinal modulus E_L = 1.1 x 14,900 = 16,390 MPa (footnote c). Wood is orthotropic; its transverse moduli are about a tenth of E_L (Table 5-1 hardwood ratios), so a tip treated as isotropic in E_L is stiffer than the real tip. Density at 12% moisture content is specific gravity x 1.12 x 1000 kg/m^3 = 806.4 kg/m^3, the convention of this repository's other FPL-GTR-282 packs. Moisture content is fixed at 12% and is not an axis of this pack. Temperature: Table 5-15 gives MOE parallel to grain at 12% moisture content +17% at -50 C and -7% at +50 C relative to 20 C, approximately linear, so about 0.24% per degree; the rows are admitted from 15 to 25 C, where that effect is within 1.2%

column3: composition-proxy: mean longitudinal-radial Poisson's ratio of the 16 hardwoods of FPL-GTR-282 Table 5-2 at about 12% moisture content
column4: Arithmetic mean of the tabulated mu_LR of ash white, aspen quaking, balsa, basswood, birch yellow, cherry black, cottonwood eastern, mahogany African, mahogany Honduras, maple sugar, maple red, oak red, oak white, sweetgum, walnut black and yellow-poplar
column5: composition-proxy: hickory is not in Table 5-2, so this is NOT a hickory measurement. The mean is 0.371 (range 0.229 to 0.495; white ash, also a drumstick wood, is 0.371). For the Hertz stick-on-film contact of the kit, the full range changes the effective modulus by about 2%

column3: composition-proxy: means of the hardwood elastic ratios of FPL-GTR-282 Table 5-1 (15 species) and Poisson's ratios of Table 5-2 (16 species) at about 12% moisture content
column4: E_T/E_L is the mean over ash white, balsa, basswood, birch yellow, cherry black, cottonwood eastern, mahogany African and Honduras, maple sugar and red, oak red and white, sweetgum, walnut black and yellow-poplar (0.05693); G_LT/E_L the same less oak white, which is untabulated (0.06657); nu_LT the Table 5-2 hardwood mean (0.4668); the transverse-plane Poisson ratio is the pack author's transversely isotropic reduction, the mean of the mu_RT (15) and mu_TR (16) hardwood means (0.5180)
column5: composition-proxy: hickory is in neither table, so these are NOT hickory measurements. They let a stick tip loaded along the grain be treated as transversely isotropic about L, with E_P = E_T and G_LP = G_LT, for the Delafargue and Ulm (2004) axial indentation modulus. The sweep over proxies (all 15 hardwoods; without balsa; white ash alone) and transverse-plane Poisson ratio 0.33 to 0.70 gives an indentation modulus of 7.1 to 8.2 GPa against 19.0 GPa for an isotropic E_L tip, E* on the PET film card of 3.17 to 3.37 GPa against 4.40 GPa, and a Hertz contact time 1.11 to 1.14 times the isotropic one

column3: Shagbark hickory (Carya ovata), a true hickory, clear straight-grained small specimens at 12% moisture content, loaded perpendicular to the grain
column4: FPL-GTR-282 Table 5-3a (metric), true hickories, 12% row: side hardness 8,400 N (footnote a: hardness measured when load is perpendicular to grain; footnote d: the true hickories' side hardness is from Bendtsen and Ethington (1975)) and compression perpendicular to grain 12,100 kPa (footnote a: fiber stress at proportional limit). Chapter 5, Strength Properties: hardness is the load required to embed a 11.28-mm (0.444-in.) ball to one-half its diameter, the average of radial and tangential penetrations; compressive stress perpendicular to grain is reported as stress at proportional limit, with no clearly defined ultimate stress
column5: Average clear-wood values, not a particular drumstick. Table 5-6 gives average coefficients of variation of 20% for side hardness and 28% for compression perpendicular to grain (the scatter of specimens, not the uncertainty of these means). The other true hickories at 12% moisture content: side hardness mockernut 8,800, pignut 9,500 and shellbark 8,100 N (stored below); compression perpendicular to grain mockernut 11,900, pignut 13,700 and shellbark 12,400 kPa. kPa converted to MPa at 1/1000. The pack stores the tabulated hardness load; read as a mean pressure over the projected area of the ball embedded to half its diameter, pi (5.64 mm)^2, it is 84.1 MPa. Temperature: Table 5-15 gives compressive strength perpendicular to grain at proportional limit -35% at +50 C relative to 20 C at 10% moisture content, about 1.2% per degree if linear, so up to about 6% over the 15 to 25 C these rows are admitted at; it tabulates no temperature effect on hardness

column3: Shagbark hickory clear wood at fixed 12 percent dry-basis moisture content
column5: Engineering correlations, not additional species measurements. Cp in J/(kg K) is 1000*((0.1031+0.003867*T+4.18*0.12)/1.12+12*(-0.06191+0.000236*T-0.000133*12)); its fixed-moisture dependence is affine in absolute T over 280-420 K, so linear interpolation reproduces this model. Transverse conductivity at 297.15 K is G12*(0.1941+0.004064*12)+0.01864 using this bundle's G12=0.72. The source restricts conductivity to G12>0.3 and MC<25 percent and reports actual conductivity may differ by 20 percent; this is not a statistical confidence interval. The new thermal claims explicitly enforce moisture content; existing mechanical claims retain their original fixed-moisture convention. No longitudinal conductivity, drying, phase change, pressure dependence, or graded-lumber qualification is supplied.
